title: The other permit systems
question: Does the same like-for-like test find consistently fast firms in electrical, plumbing, Fire, Planning and Public Works permits, and are any fast in more than one?
finding: Electrical and plumbing permits leave almost no room for a fast lane: 96% and 97% are issued the day they are filed, and only 1 and 1 of 821 and 914 contractors tested meet the test. Where waits exist the test finds firms on both sides. Fire Department permits: 8 consistently faster and 10 consistently slower of 82 tested; Planning cases: 1 consistently faster and 4 consistently slower of 28 tested; Public Works street permits: 19 consistently faster and 49 consistently slower of 157 tested. 1 firm is consistently fast in two or more systems (B-Side Inc.), and none of the firms that are consistently fast on building permits is also consistently fast in another system. The three largest filers of street permits: Pacific Gas and Electric (6,862 filing days, faster on 58%); J. Flores Construction Company Inc (2,239 filing days, faster on 55%); PODS, Inc (1,820 filing days, faster on 54%).
how: The same test as for building permits, with cells that fit each system. Electrical and plumbing: days from filing to issue among permits of the same series (counter or online), value band and filing year, by licensed contractor. Fire Department permits: days from application to approval among permits of the same type and year, by permit holder. Planning cases: days from opening to closing among cases of the same kind (conditional use, historic-building approval, large-project approval, project application, variance; project applications are also split into new buildings, additions, changes of use and other) and year, by the applicant's firm, with withdrawn and cancelled cases left out. Public Works street permits: the City publishes the approval date but no application date. Assuming permit numbers are given out in order of application within a year and series (the numbering fits that reading but no published document states it), each permit was applied for no later than the earliest approval among later-numbered permits; approval minus that date is an estimated wait, compared among permits of the same type and year, by the firm the permit was issued to. City departments are left out as applicants. Same floors and the same rule for the cut in each system.
limits: An electrical or plumbing permit is nearly always issued on the day, so the handful of firms that stand out there differ from like permits by a few points only. 75% of the Fire Department permits compared are of types described as temporary or for an event, and the wait may measure how early the caterer or promoter applied as much as how fast the department answered. A Planning case may be slow because the project is large or contested, which the cells capture only roughly; firms that take hard cases will look slow. The street-permit wait rests on an assumption (that numbers are given out in order of application), is an estimate and a lower bound, and is fair between neighbours in the queue but not exact. Firms are joined across systems on licence number or exact normalised name, so a firm that trades under two names is missed. Approvals by the Board of Supervisors are a separate system; their speed by vendor and by sponsor is tested in the screens 'Whose files pass fastest and slowest' and 'Board speed by sponsor' of the group 'The same winners, year after year' and is not repeated here.

columns.t: Share faster than the like-permit median
